questions.question:
In which Five-year plan was the following statement quoted?

“The urge to bring economic and social change under present conditions comes from the fact of poverty and inequalities in income, wealth and opportunity”.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First Five-year plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement "The urge to bring economic and social change under present conditions comes from the fact of poverty and inequalities in income, wealth, and opportunity" was quoted in the context of the **First Five-Year Plan** in India.
 
• This plan, spanning from **1951 to 1956**, emphasized **economic development and the eradication of poverty **through a centralized planning approach.
 
• It aimed to address socioeconomic disparities and lay the foundation for India's industrialization and modernization.
 
• The First Five Year Plan delineated the trajectory of economic development in India, spearheading significant initiatives.
 
• Presented by India's inaugural Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru,** it was formally introduced to the Parliament of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan** placed a strong emphasis on rapid industrialization and the expansion of the public sector. It was formulated under the guidance of renowned economist P.C. Mahalanobis.
 
• **The Third Five-Year Plan**, implemented from 1961 to 1966, marked a shift towards a centralized and comprehensive national economic strategy aimed at fostering development across various sectors.
 
• **The Fourth Five-Year Plan**, spanning from 1969 to 1974, was structured based on the Gadgil Formula. This plan aimed to promote economic growth while ensuring stability and self-reliance. Its objectives included the development of agriculture, industry, and infrastructure to foster balanced and sustainable progress.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers is credited with the construction of Purana Quila in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun and Sher Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Purana Quila,** situated in** Delhi, India,** was jointly constructed by the **second Mughal Emperor, Humayun, **and the **Afghan King, Sher Shah Suri.**
 
• Although Humayun initiated its construction, Sher Shah Suri contributed several structures to the fort. Dating back to the** 16th century, **the Purana Quila stands as one of Delhi's oldest forts.
 
• Functioning as the inner citadel of the **city of Dinpanah**, the fort is positioned near the Pragati Maidan exhibition ground. Its walls, towering at 18 meters in height, extend over a length of 1 to 5 kilometers.
 
• Throughout its history, the Purana Quila has borne witness to the rise and fall of empires and the reign of mighty rulers.
 
• Sher Shah Suri is credited with the creation of several interior structures within the fort, notably the **Qila-i-Kuhn mosque and the Sher Mandal.**
 
• These architectural elements add to the historical significance and grandeur of the Purana Quila.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nasir al-Din Muhammad,** known by his regnal name Humayun, served as the second Mughal emperor, reigning over territories encompassing present-day Eastern Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Northern India, and Pakistan.
 
• His rule extended from 1530 to 1540 and was interrupted, only to be restored from 1555 until his passing in 1556. By the time of his death, the Mughal Empire had expanded to cover nearly one million square kilometers.
 
• **Sher Shah Suri,** often hailed as the "Just King," emerged as the founder of the Sur Empire in India. Initially serving as regent and later assuming sole rulership of Bihar from 1529 to 1540, he rose to prominence by defeating the Mughal Empire in 1540. T
 
• his victory led to the establishment of the Sur Empire, with Delhi as its capital, and Sher Shah Suri declaring himself Emperor. Following his accidental demise in 1545 CE, his son, Islam Shah, succeeded him as ruler.

questions.question: Which of the following traditional dances is mainly performed during Navaratri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Garba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Garba,** a traditional Gujarati folk dance, is performed during the** nine-day Hindu festival** of** Navaratri**.
 
• It is a ritualistic and devotional dance paying homage to Durga, representing the cyclical nature of time.
 
• Participants form a circle around a clay lantern called a Garbha Deep, symbolizing life, while accompanied by live orchestras or devotional songs.
 
• Garba portrays the nine-day battle between Goddess Durga and Mahishasura, symbolizing the victory of good over evil during Navratri.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **The Ras Leela**, alternatively referred to as the Rasalila or Ras dance, is an age-old Indian folk dance portraying the enchanting narrative of Krishna, Radha, and the gopis.
 
• **Nati**, originating from the upper Himachal region of India, encompasses both dance and song, sharing the same name.
 
• **Dumhal,** a classical folk dance, is executed by the male members of the Wattal tribe hailing from the picturesque Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.question: When was the Duckworth-Lewis formula used for the first time in international cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 January 1997**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Duckworth-Lewis (D/L) method, **also referred to as the **Duckworth–Lewis–Stern (DLS) method**, made its** debut in international cricket** during a match between **Zimbabwe and England in 1997.**
 
• Subsequently, the **International Cricket Council (ICC) **formally embraced the D/L method in 1999.
 
• This method is a mathematical formula designed to determine revised targets for cricket matches disrupted by rain.
 
• It takes into account both the number of overs and wickets remaining as key resources and adjusts the target accordingly based on their availability.
 
• Renowned for its fairness and objectivity, the D/L method relies on historical data and is relatively straightforward to calculate, even without the aid of a computer.
 
• Its adaptability makes it a valuable tool for ensuring equitable outcomes in rain-affected cricket matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Duckworth-Lewis (D/L) method** was originally formulated by** two English statisticians, Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis.**
 
• In 2015, the method was updated by Australian academic Steve Stern. This method is employed in all international and domestic limited-overs cricket matches, including Twenty20 matches.
 
• It serves as a standardized mechanism for calculating revised targets in matches affected by weather interruptions, ensuring fairness and objectivity in such situations.

questions.question: Choose from the following the novel written by Salman Rushdie.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Satanic Verses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"The Satanic Verses"** is the** fourth novel** penned by** British-Indian author Salman Rushdie**.
 
• Initially published in** September 1988,** the narrative draws inspiration from the life of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
 
• Employing his characteristic style, Rushdie blends elements of magical realism with contemporary events and figures to craft his characters.
 
• The title of the novel alludes to the** "Satanic Verses," **a collection of Quranic verses referencing three pagan Meccan goddesses: Allāt, Al-Uzza, and Manāt.
 
• This aspect of the story is rooted in accounts from historians such as al-Waqidi and al-Tabari. Upon its release, "The Satanic Verses" garnered significant attention and acclaim.
 
• It emerged as a finalist for the **1988 Booker Prize**, ultimately conceding to Peter Carey's "Oscar and Lucinda." Nevertheless, Rushdie's work secured the 1988 Whitbread Award for Novel of the Year, solidifying its place as a celebrated piece of literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Salman Rushdie **is an Indian-born British-American novelist renowned for his distinctive blend of magic realism and historical fiction.
 
• His literary themes frequently explore the interplay, disruptions, and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations, with a particular focus on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Rushdie's second novel, "Midnight's Children" (1981), achieved widespread acclaim and secured the prestigious Booker Prize in 1981.
 
• It was twice recognized as "the best novel of all winners" on the 25th and 40th anniversaries of the prize, underscoring its enduring significance in the literary landscape.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly define the way the unemployment rate is calculated in India?

options.text: The percentage of persons unemployed among the persons in the labour force
The percentage of persons unemployed among the total population
The percentage of persons in labour force
The percentage of employed persons in the population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The percentage of persons unemployed among the persons in the labour force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The unemployment rate** represents the **proportion of unemployed** individuals within the** labor force.**
 
• **The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS),** conducted by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO),** serves as a tool to gauge the unemployment rate in urban areas.
 
• According to the PLFS, unemployment rate is calculated as the percentage of unemployed individuals among those considered to be part of the labor force.
 
• Data from the PLFS indicates a decline in the urban unemployment rate in India from 7.2% in July–September 2022 to 6.6% in July–September 2023.
 
• Furthermore, in October–December 2023, the urban unemployment rate dropped to its lowest level in over four years, reaching 6.5%.
 
• Additionally, the unemployment rate among females in India exhibited a decrease from 9.1% in April–June 2023 to 8.6% in July–September 2023.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Worker Population Ratio (WPR)** is the **percentage of people employed** within the population.
 
• In the period of 2022-2023, there was a notable increase in the WPR across rural and urban areas in India. Specifically, in rural regions, the WPR rose from 44.8% to 54.2%, while in urban areas, it increased from 42.6% to 46.0%.
 
• Moreover, there were significant improvements observed in the WPR among both men and women in India.
 
• For men, the WPR escalated from 68.6% in 2017-18 to 73.5% in 2022-23, indicating a substantial increase. Similarly, for women, the WPR surged from 19.2% to 30.0% during the same period, reflecting notable progress in female employment rates.

questions.question: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty Seventh Amendment) Bill, 2021, was introduced in the Lok Sabha by the ______ in August 2021.

options.text: Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty Seventh Amendment) Bill, 2021, **was introduced in the** Lok Sabha by the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment **in **August 2021.**
 
• The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Seventh Amendment) Bill, 2021, presented in the Lok Sabha by Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment,** Dr. Virendra Kumar, **on August 9, 2021, proposes an amendment to the Constitution to authorize states and** union territories** to formulate their own roster of socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• **The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)** was established pursuant to the National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993.
 
• The Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018 conferred constitutional status upon the NCBC, granting the President the authority to publish the roster of socially and educationally backward classes for any state or union territory for all intents and purposes.
 
• The 2021 Bill seeks to amend this provision, specifying that the President may publish the roster of socially and educationally backward classes solely for the purposes of the central government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, **a ministry under the Government of India, is tasked with overseeing the welfare, social justice, and empowerment of marginalized and disadvantaged segments of society.
 
• This includes scheduled castes (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), LGBT individuals, persons with disabilities, the elderly, and victims of drug abuse.
 
• The ministry plays a pivotal role in implementing legislation aimed at safeguarding the rights of these marginalized groups and ensuring the effective enforcement of anti-discrimination policies.
 
• The Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment holds cabinet rank as a member of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Currently, the ministry is led by Virendra Kumar, who is supported by Ministers of State, including Rattan Lal Kataria, Krishan Pal Gujjar, and Ramdas Athavale.

questions.question: Which of the following food items can be used as natural food preservatives?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Garlic, lemon, sugar and vinegar__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Garlic, lemon, sugar, and vinegar **are renowned for their multifaceted roles in** food preservation**.
 
• **Garlic's allicin content, lemon's citric acid, sugar's ability to reduce water activity, and vinegar's acetic acid** create a formidable arsenal against microbial growth.
 
• Their combined effect extends **beyond mere preservation, enhancing flavors and textures **while safeguarding against spoilage.
 
• From pickling to marinating, these natural agents infuse foods with both preservation and culinary prowess. Yet, their historical significance transcends mere utility, reflecting a profound understanding of nature's bounty and the artistry of culinary tradition.
 
• As guardians of flavor and longevity, they bridge the gap between past wisdom and contemporary culinary innovation, ensuring that the legacy of natural food preservation endures with every tangy bite and savory morsel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Natural food preservatives**, derived from sources like plants, minerals, and microorganisms, play a vital role in extending the shelf life of food products while maintaining their quality and safety.
 
• **Salt,** a time-honored preservative, works by drawing out moisture, inhibiting bacterial growth, and preserving meats, fish, and vegetables.
 
• Similarly, **sugar**, in forms such as sucrose, honey, or molasses, reduces water activity, impeding microbial proliferation in jams, jellies, and preserves.
 
• **Vinegar,** rich in acetic acid, creates an acidic environment hostile to bacteria and molds, making it indispensable in pickling and salad dressings.
 
• **Citric acid,** abundant in citrus fruits, acts as a preservative by preventing microbial growth in canned goods and beverages.
 
• Meanwhile, **rosemary extract**, rich in natural antioxidants, serves as a preservative while imparting flavor and maintaining product integrity.
 
• These natural preservatives not only ensure food safety but also reflect a commitment to harnessing nature's bounty for sustainable food preservation practices.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Depressed Classes Association, in 1930?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. BR Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** founded the **Depressed Classes Association** in **August 1930** with the aim of improving the social and economic status of marginalized communities.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi **initiated the **Civil Disobedience Movement** in March 1930, starting with the **Salt Satyagraha** to protest against the salt tax imposed by the **British colonial government.**
 
• The movement concluded in March 1931 with the signing of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
 
• In December 1929, during the session of the Indian National Congress held in Lahore, the historic 'Purna Swaraj' resolution was adopted.
 
• This resolution declared complete independence (Swaraj) from British rule as the primary objective of the Indian freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** was a prominent Indian jurist, economist, social reformer, and political leader.
 
• He played a pivotal role in various spheres of Indian society and governance. Ambedkar led the committee responsible for drafting the Constitution of India during the Constituent Assembly debates.
 
• Additionally, he served as the Law and Justice Minister in the inaugural cabinet of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. A champion of social justice, Ambedkar inspired the Dalit Buddhist movement after renouncing Hinduism, advocating for the rights and dignity of marginalized communities.
 
• In recognition of his immense contributions to Indian society, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was posthumously conferred with the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1990.
 
• His legacy continues to resonate deeply in India's ongoing pursuit of equality and social reform.

questions.question: The famous tripartite struggle was fought for control over ________ in early medieval period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannauj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tripartite Struggle,** commonly referred to as the **Kannauj Triangle Wars,** transpired in the ninth century, revolving around the **battle for dominance in northern India** among three prominent empires**: the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire, the Pala Empire, and the Rashtrakuta Empire.**
 
• This intense conflict primarily revolved around asserting control over the city of Kannauj, which served as a pivotal symbol of authority over the Ganges plain.
 
• During this period, the** Palas of Bengal, the Pratiharas of Central India, and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan** engaged in fierce warfare to secure their influence over Kannauj.
 
• Ultimately, the Pratiharas emerged as the triumphant force, consolidating their power and dominance in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kannauj, **located in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, serves as both a city and an administrative center, functioning as a municipal board or Nagar Palika Parishad within Kannauj district. The name "Kannauj" is an evolved form of the classical name "Kanyakubja".
 
• Historically, it was also known as "Mahodaya" during the reign of Mihira Bhoja. Positioned 104 kilometers west of the state capital, Lucknow, Kannauj has been a significant center throughout Classical India, serving as a focal point for various imperial Indian dynasties.
 
• Among these dynasties, the earliest was the Maukhari dynasty, followed by Emperor Harsha of the Vardhana dynasty. Subsequently, Kannauj came under the rule of the Gahadavala dynasty, attaining unprecedented glory under the reign of Govindachandra.

questions.question: Which festival celebrated by Muslims is also known as Barawafat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milad-un-Nabi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barawafat,** also known as **Eid-e-Milad-un-Nabi,** is a festival observed to commemorate** the birth and death of Prophet Muhammad.**
 
• It falls on the 12th day of Rabi ul Awal, the month believed to be the **birth month of the Prophet**. The name Barawafat is derived from the Urdu words "bara," meaning twelve, and "wafat," meaning death.
 
• This festival holds immense significance for Muslims worldwide. It serves as a day of reflection on the teachings of the Prophet, with large gatherings convened where religious poems are recited, and discussions about the Prophet's virtues are conducted.
 
• Barawafat is celebrated with variations between Shia and Sunni communities, each observing the occasion in accordance with their respective traditions and customs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Muharram** marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar and is recognized as the Islamic New Year.
 
• **Eid al-Adha**, also known as the Feast of Sacrifice, is one of the two primary holidays celebrated in Islam. It commemorates the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son, Ishmael, as an act of obedience to God's command.
 
• **Shab-e-Barat **is a cultural observance occurring on the 15th night of Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Islamic calendar.

questions.question: What will be the focal length of a convex lens with the power of a +2.5 Diopter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**40 cm**__.

***__Key Points__**

The **formula to calculate the focal length **** �** f of a lens in meters using its power � P *in diopters is:

f = {1over P}

Given that the power P = +2.5 diopters, we can substitute it into the formula:

f = {1over 2.5}

***f* = 0.4 m**

So, the focal length of the convex lens is 0.4 m or **40 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **The focal length of a convex lens **denotes the distance from the lens's center to its focus, indicating the lens's ability to converge or diverge light.
 
• It is consistently positive for convex lenses.
 
• The lens formula, expressed as **1/f = 1/v - 1/u, **determines the focal length, where v represents the distance between the image and the lens, and u represents the distance between the object and the lens.

questions.question: Nagarjuni Caves were donated to which of the following sects by Mauryans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajivika**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ajivikas sect **received the **Nagarjuni Caves** as a gift from the **Mauryans.**
 
• An earlier Indian philosophical and religious sect that **opposed Jainism **was called the **Ajivikas.**
 
• In 261 BC, the four caves on **Barabar hill **were given to the Ajivika monks by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka.
 
• The grandson and successor of Ashoka, **Dasaratha Maurya,** also dedicated the caverns to the Ajivikas.
 
• Situated on** Nagarjuni hill, 1.6 kilometers east of the Barabar caverns,** are the caverns. Named Gopika, Vadathika, and Vapiyaka, these are the three caves located on Nagarjuni hill.
 
• The caverns were created in the third century BC, during Ashoka and his son Dasaratha Maurya's Mauryan dynasty.
 
• The caves served as homes for the Ajivikas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Due to the popularity of the **Ajivika faith,** Buddhism was seen as being seriously threatened by the Ajivikas by the first century BCE.
 
• Under the support of the Nanda and Mauryan rulers, the Ajivikas flourished but experienced a dramatic decline thereafter.
 
• The Ajivika faith disappeared entirely after the fourteenth century.

questions.question: Who became India’s second highest wicket taker in Tests after Anil Kumble by taking his 435th test wicket in March 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravichandran Ashwin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ravichandran Ashwin **has climbed to become **India's second-highest wicket-taker in Test cricket,** following the legendary **Anil Kumble**, after securing his** 435th test wicket.**
 
• Prior to this, he had matched **Kapil Dev's record of 434 Test wickets**.
 
• Ashwin reached this milestone by dismissing** Sri Lankan batsman Pathum Nissanka** on Day 3 of the ongoing first Test between **India and Sri Lanka at the PCA Stadium **in Mohali on** March 6, 2022.**
 
• With this achievement, he now stands as the ninth highest wicket-taker in the history of Test cricket.
 
• Just a day earlier, the off-spinner had surpassed New Zealand's bowling great Richard Hadlee, elevating him to the 11th position among Test cricket's leading wicket-takers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ravichandran Ashwin**, a right-arm off-spin bowler and a lower-order batsman, is widely acclaimed as one of the most proficient off-spinners in cricket history.
 
• He represents the Indian national cricket team and was a vital member of the squads that clinched the 2011 Cricket World Cup and the 2013 Champions Trophy.
 
• Ashwin also competes for Tamil Nadu and South Zone in domestic cricket and plies his trade for the Rajasthan Royals in the Indian Premier League (IPL). With 500 wickets in Test cricket, Ashwin holds the distinction of being the quickest bowler to reach 300 wickets in terms of the number of innings.
 
• He made his Test debut against the West Indies in 2011, becoming the seventh Indian bowler to claim a five-wicket haul on debut.
 
• Renowned for his stellar performances, Ashwin has been named to the** ICC Men's Test Team of the Year on five occasions **and was selected in the ICC Men's Test Team of the Decade for the period 2011–2020.
 
• In recognition of his contributions to cricket, he was honored with the **Arjuna Award **by the Government of India in 2015.

questions.question: The name of Bhajan Sopori is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Bhajan Sopori **was a prominent Indian instrumentalist renowned for his mastery of the **santoor, **an ancient stringed musical instrument.
 
• He belonged to the **Sufiana gharana,** a revered lineage within Indian classical music.
 
• Often regarded as a cultural bridge between Jammu and Kashmir and the rest of India, Pandit Sopori established the SaMaPa (Sopori Academy for Music and Performing Arts) music academy, dedicated to promoting Indian classical music.
 
• Pandit Sopori's contributions to music were widely recognized and honored. He received prestigious accolades such as the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1992**, the **Padma Shri in 2004**, and the **Baba Allaudin Khan Award in 2009.**
 
• He was the recipient of the M N Mathur Award in 2011 for his significant contributions to Indian classical music. In recognition of his lifelong dedication and achievements, he was also honored with the Jammu and Kashmir State Lifetime Achievement Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indian santoor **is a** trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer**, influenced by the **Iranian santur.**
 
• Typically crafted from walnut wood, it features 25 bridges. Each bridge supports 4 strings, resulting in a total of 100 strings.
 
• This traditional instrument has deep roots in the culture of Jammu and Kashmir and boasts ancient origins.
 
• In ancient Sanskrit texts, it was referred to as the Shatha Tantri Veena.

questions.question: Vasanta Ritu falls in which months, according to the Gregorian Calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**March-April**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Hindu calendar, Vasant Ritu, **or spring, spans the months of **Chaitra and Baisakh**, which approximately align with mid-**February to mid-April **on the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Vasant Ritu is widely regarded as one of the most picturesque seasons in India, characterized by pleasant weather and maximum temperatures typically reaching around 32°C.
 
• **During Vasant Ritu**, several significant Hindu festivals are celebrated across the country.
 
• These festivals include Vasant Panchami, Ugadi, Gudi Padwa, Holi, Rama Navami, Vishu, Bihu, Baisakhi, Puthandu, and Hanuman Jayanti.
 
• These festivities mark the onset of spring and are observed with great enthusiasm and fervor by people of Hindu faith throughout India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In** Sanskrit, "Vasanta" translates to spring. "Panchami" **refers to the fifth day of the Shukla Paksha, the bright fortnight of the waxing moon, in the Hindu month of Magha, which typically falls in January to February.
 
• **Vasanta Panchami, **celebrated on this day, symbolizes the conclusion of winter and the advent of spring.
 
• This auspicious occasion is dedicated to the worship of the goddess Saraswati, who embodies knowledge, wisdom, and the arts.

questions.question: Which stone could convert all baser metals like iron into gold?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Philosopher’s stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In Western alchemy, the philosopher's stone** is a mysterious substance believed to possess the **extraordinary ability to transform** base metals like iron into precious gold.
 
• Also referred to as **"the tincture" or "the powder,"** this elusive stone was thought to hold immense power beyond mere transmutation.
 
• Alchemists held the belief that the philosopher's stone could remedy ailments, bestow eternal youth, and even grant immortality. Contrary to its name, the philosopher's stone was not a physical rock but was believed to exist in various forms such as a magical wax, liquid, or powder.
 
• The philosopher's stone occupied a central place in the esoteric language of alchemy, embodying ideals of perfection, divine enlightenment, and celestial joy.
 
• The pursuit of uncovering the philosopher's stone was encapsulated in the concept known as the Magnum Opus, or "Great Work," representing the alchemist's quest for ultimate knowledge and transformation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Emerald** is a gemstone that belongs to the beryl mineral family and is distinguished by its vibrant green hue, which is attributed to the presence of trace amounts of chromium or, in some cases, vanadium.
 
• **Jade** is a broad term encompassing two distinct types of ornamental rocks: nephrite and jadeite. These stones are highly valued for their beauty and durability, and they are commonly utilized in jewelry, decorative items, and various other applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Constitutional Body in India?

options.text: Union Public Service Commission of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Human Rights Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **State Human Rights Commission** is** NOT** a** Constitutional Body in India.**
 
• **The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC)** in India is** an independent body **tasked with **safeguarding and promoting human rights **at the **state level.**
 
• Established under the **Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993,** the SHRC is empowered with several key functions:
 
 
• **Intervention in Human Rights Violations:** The SHRC holds the authority to intervene in any instance involving a breach of human rights.
 
• **Review and Protection of Human Rights: **The SHRC is responsible for reviewing and ensuring the protection of human rights within its jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• It's important to note that the SHRC can only investigate violations of human rights falling under the State List (List-II) and the Concurrent List (List-III) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **As of December 2011**, 20 states, including Rajasthan, had established their respective SHRCs.
 
• In Rajasthan, the chairperson and members of the State Human Rights Commission serve a term of three years or until they reach the age of 70, whichever comes first.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Election Commission of India** is a constitutional body mandated by the Constitution of India to oversee and regulate elections throughout the country.
 
• **The State Public Service Commission (SPSC)** is another constitutional body responsible for organizing examinations and interviews to select candidates for various state civil administrative services.
 
• **The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is also a constitutional entity entrusted with the task of conducting direct recruitment examinations to appoint officers to the prestigious All India Services and the Central Civil Services (Group A and B).

questions.question: Name the hot, dry oppressing winds that blow in between Delhi and Patna.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The hot, dry, and oppressive winds **that sweep** between Delhi and Patna** are referred to as **Loo.**
 
• These winds are characterized by their strength, gustiness, and dustiness, and they typically occur during the daytime across northern and northwestern India.
 
• Particularly intense during the months of **May and June, temperatures **can soar to** 45–50 °C **(115–120 °F) during their presence.
 
• Originating from the Iranian, Baloch, and Thar deserts, Loo winds primarily emanate from the scorching Thar desert.
 
• They commonly manifest in the afternoons, contributing to the sweltering conditions experienced in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mango Showers,** prevalent in the states of Karnataka and Kerala, are pre-monsoon showers occurring before the onset of the monsoon season.
 
• **Nor'westers, **also called kalbaisakhis, are localized thunderstorms and rainfall events that commonly happen in Indian states like Jharkhand, Assam, Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar, and Tripura, as well as in Bangladesh, during the summer months.
 
• **Blossom showers,** a natural occurrence, take place during the spring season.

questions.question: How many Directive Principles were added or amended in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The 42nd Amendment to the Indian Constitution**, enacted in **1976, **introduced significant changes, including the addition of four new directive principles.
 
• These directive principles are guidelines for the state to follow while formulating policies and laws, aiming to establish a just and equitable society.
 
• **Four Directive Principles** were added by the 42nd Amendment as follows:
 
• **Article 39:** This directive principle emphasizes that the state should direct its policies towards securing social justice and equality. It highlights several aspects, including equitable distribution of resources, prevention of concentration of wealth and means of production, and ensuring that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and resources.
 
• **Article 39A: **This principle focuses on providing free legal aid and ensuring that justice is not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities. It aims to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not inaccessible to economically disadvantaged sections of society.
 
• **Article 43A: **This directive principle relates to participation of workers in management of industries. It emphasizes that the state shall take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments, or other organizations engaged in any industry.
 
• **Article 48A: **This principle pertains to protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife. It mandates that the state shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.

questions.question: The Election Commission of India was established in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Election Commission of India **was established in **1950**.
 
• **The Election Commission of India (ECI) **is a **constitutional body **established by the **Constitution of India **with the **mandate to oversee and regulate elections **throughout the country.
 
• **Article 324** of the Constitution empowers the Election Commission with the authority and responsibility for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to various offices, including parliament, state legislatures, the presidency, and the vice presidency.
 
• As such, the Election Commission functions as a nationwide entity, serving **both the Central government and the state governments**.
 
• This esteemed body administers elections for a multitude of governmental positions, including the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, State Legislative Councils, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President of the nation.
 
• The Election Commission operates within the framework provided by the Constitution, as stipulated in Article 324, and implements relevant electoral laws such as the Representation of the People Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Established in 1950, the Election Commission initially comprised only** one Chief Election Commissioner.**
 
• However, on **October 16, 1989, ahead of the 1989 General Election,** two additional Commissioners were appointed, albeit for a brief period until January 1, 1990.
 
• Subsequently, the** Election Commissioner Amendment Act, 1989,** was enacted, transforming the commission into a multi-member body. Since then, a three-member Commission has been operational, with decisions made through majority voting.
 
• Situated in New Delhi, the commission is supported by its secretariat. Assisting the Election Commissioners are Deputy Election Commissioners, typically comprising Indian Administrative Service officers.
 
• **Rajiv Kumar**, a former Indian Administrative Service officer born on February 19, 1960, assumed office as the 25th Chief Election Commissioner of India on May 15, 2022, succeeding Sushil Chandra.
